question: Solve the system \(\{2x+y-z=6,\ x-y+z=0,\ x+y+z=6\}\). (Give the values of \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\), in this order, separated by commas.)
solution: Adding the first and second equations gives \(3x=6\), so \(x=2\). Subtracting the second equation from the third gives \(2y=6\), so \(y=3\). Substituting into the third equation gives \(z=6-2-3=1\).

Adding/subtracting equations is performed to find their common solutions, not unrelated separate equation values.
